nodes.title: Formulation of LPP & Key Terms
points: Linear Programming Problem (LPP) optimizes (maximizes or minimizes) a linear objective function subject to linear constraints.
Decision Variables: x, y (quantities to be determined, always non-negative: x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0).
Objective Function: Z = ax + by, where a, b are constants representing profit/cost per unit.
Constraints: Linear inequalities representing restrictions on resources: a₁x + b₁y ≤ c₁ or a₂x + b₂y ≥ c₂.
Non-negativity restrictions: x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 restrict the feasible region strictly to the FIRST QUADRANT.

nodes.title: Graphical Representation of Inequations
points: Convert each inequation ax + by ≤ c into equality ax + by = c to find line intercepts: put y = 0 ⟹ x = c/a; put x = 0 ⟹ y = c/b.
Origin Test: Substitute (0, 0) into inequation. If statement is true (e.g., 0 ≤ 10), shade region CONTAINING origin. If false (e.g., 0 ≥ 10), shade region AWAY from origin.
If line passes through origin (c = 0), test with (1, 0) or (0, 1) instead.
Inclusive inequalities (≤, ≥): Draw solid boundary lines. Strict inequalities (<, >): Draw dashed boundary lines.

nodes.title: Feasible Region & Feasible Solutions
points: Solution: Any point (x, y) satisfying the given conditions.
Feasible Solution: Any point (x, y) that satisfies ALL constraints and non-negativity restrictions simultaneously.
Feasible Region (Solution Set): The common region determined by all inequalities simultaneously.
Convex Polygon: A region where the line segment joining any two points in the region lies entirely inside the region. The feasible region of an LPP is ALWAYS a convex polygon.
Bounded vs Unbounded: Bounded feasible region can be enclosed in a circle; unbounded extends indefinitely.

nodes.title: Corner Point Method (Vertex Theorem)
points: Fundamental Theorem of LPP: If a feasible region is bounded, the optimum (maximum or minimum) value of objective function Z occurs at one of the CORNER POINTS (vertices) of the feasible region.
Steps of Corner Point Method:
1. Find all corner points of the feasible region by solving intersecting boundary lines pairwise.
2. Construct a table listing each corner point (x, y) and evaluate Z = ax + by.
3. Select the maximum or minimum value of Z from the table.
If the optimum value occurs at two adjacent vertices, it occurs at EVERY point on the line segment joining them.

formulas.label: Optimum value location
formulas.expr: Z_opt occurs at a vertex (x_i, y_i)

nodes.title: Multiple Optimal Solutions & Infeasibility
points: Multiple Optimal Solutions: Occur when the objective function line Z = ax + by is PARALLEL to a boundary edge of the feasible region (i.e., slope −a/b equals slope of boundary line), and both vertices of that edge give the same optimum value. In this case, infinite optimal solutions exist along that edge.
Infeasible LPP: Occurs when there is NO common feasible region satisfying all constraints simultaneously (empty solution set).
Unbounded Objective Value: Occurs when the feasible region is unbounded and Z can increase or decrease indefinitely.

formulas.label: Multiple optimal condition
formulas.expr: Slope of Z = Slope of boundary edge

nodes.title: Unbounded Feasible Region Protocol
points: When the feasible region is unbounded:
Step 1: Compute M = maximum value of Z at corner points.
Step 2: Plot the open half-plane ax + by > M.
Step 3: If this open half-plane has NO common points with the feasible region, M is the true maximum. If it has common points, Z has NO maximum (unbounded).
For minimization: Compute m = minimum value of Z. Check open half-plane ax + by < m.

formulas.label: Unbounded Max test
formulas.expr: Half-plane ax + by > M has no common points

formulas.label: Unbounded Min test
formulas.expr: Half-plane ax + by < m has no common points

nodes.title: Standard LPP Word Problems
points: Manufacturing Problem: Maximize profit Z subject to machine hours, labor hours, and material constraints (typically ≤ type).
Diet Problem: Minimize cost Z subject to minimum nutritional requirements (typically ≥ type).
Allocation / Transport Problem: Optimize resources across distribution centers.
Translation tip: 'At least k' ⟹ ≥ k; 'At most k' ⟹ ≤ k; 'Not more than k' ⟹ ≤ k; 'Not less than k' ⟹ ≥ k.

nodes.title: Iso-Profit & Iso-Cost Method
points: An Iso-Profit (or Iso-Cost) line is the locus of points (x, y) giving a constant value of Z: ax + by = c.
All iso-profit lines are parallel to each other with slope m = −a/b.
For maximization: Move the iso-profit line outward (away from origin) until it just touches the farthest vertex of the feasible region.
For minimization: Move the line inward (towards origin) until it touches the nearest vertex of the feasible region.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Presentation Protocol
points: Standard 4-Mark Board Steps:
1. State decision variables clearly (Let x = units of A, y = units of B).
2. Formulate objective function Z and system of inequalities.
3. Make intercept table for each line: (x, 0) and (0, y).
4. Draw neat graph on graph paper / answer sheet with labeled axes, line equations, and shaded feasible region.
5. Find corner point coordinates by solving intersecting equations.
6. Construct Corner Point Table evaluating Z at every vertex and state: 'Maximum value of Z is ... at point (x, y)'.

formulas.label: Corner point table
formulas.expr: Point | Coordinates (x, y) | Value of Z

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, 15-Second Hacks & Redundant Constraints
points: Redundant Constraint Trick: If a constraint's line lies entirely outside the feasible region formed by other constraints, it has NO effect on the optimal solution.
15-Second Corner Evaluation: Usually, maximum occurs at the intersection of the two most restrictive constraints (lines with highest cost/profit trade-offs).
Parallel Slope Hack: If slope of Z equals slope of one of the constraints, the problem has MULTIPLE OPTIMAL SOLUTIONS instantly.
Origin Trap: Never forget x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0. If negative values are included, the solution is completely invalid.
Minimization Diet Problem: Usually bounded from below; minimum occurs at one of the outer corner points.
